questions.question: Define hydel tourism. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Define hydel tourism. [K] / [CO1]
  • Hydel tourism is a form of special-interest tourism that combines visiting hydropower projects with
  • recreational water-based activities. It involves tourists exploring dams and powerhouses, enjoying activities
  • like boating, river rafting, and kayaking in the surrounding water bodies, and learning about hydroelectric
  • power generation.
  • Core components: Hydel tourism centers are often located at or near hydroelectric power plants and their
  • associated reservoirs, which serve as tourist attractions.
  • Activities: Common activities include tours of the power plant and dam, boating, and other water sports like
  • river rafting and kayaking.
  • Purpose: It serves the dual purpose of providing a unique tourism experience and promoting public
  • awareness about hydroelectric power projects and sustainable energy.
  • Economic and social benefits: It can also generate socio-economic benefits for local communities in remote
  • areas where these projects are located.

questions.question: Why preliminary assessment important in ecotourism planning. / [CO4, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Why preliminary assessment important in ecotourism planning. [U] / [CO4, CO5]
  • A preliminary assessment is crucial in ecotourism planning because it helps determine the
  • feasibility and sustainability of a project by evaluating potential environmental impacts,
  • identifying suitable locations, and engaging stakeholders
  • Reasonsforconductingapreliminaryassessment:
  • Ensures feasibility: It determines if an ecotourism project is possible and viable by assessing
  • both the natural and economic potential of an area.
  • Identifies risks and opportunities: Tools like SWOT analysis (Strengths, Weaknesses,
  • Opportunities, Threats) can be used to understand a community's readiness for development,
  • identify potential problems, and uncover opportunities for growth.
  • Protects fragile ecosystems: It helps identify and avoid developing in areas that are too fragile
  • to withstand tourism, thereby minimizing negative environmental impacts.
  • Includes community and stakeholders: It involves identifying and engaging all relevant
  • stakeholders, including local communities, to ensure that their needs and concerns are
  • addressed from the outset.
  • Providesafoundationforsustainableplans : The information gathered is essential for
  • creating informed, scientifically-based plans that support both conservation and community
  • well-being.

questions.question: Discuss the eco-friendly practices commonly found in ecotourism centers. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the eco-friendly practices commonly found in ecotourism centers. [U] / [CO1]
  • Eco-friendly ecotourism centers commonly implement practices like using renewable energy, managing waste
  • responsibly through recycling and reduction, conserving water, and constructing eco-lodges with minimal
  • environmental impact. They also focus on conservation through guided tours, educating visitors on local
  • ecosystems, and ensuring that tourism benefits local communities economically and culturally.
  • Environmentalandinfrastructurepractices
  •  Renewable energy: Utilizing solar, wind, or other renewable sources for power and using energy-
  • efficient appliances and lighting.
  •  Waste management: Implementing strong policies for waste reduction, separation, and recycling, and
  • discouraging single-use plastics.
  •  Water conservation: Implementing water-saving measures and rainwater harvesting systems.
  •  Sustainable construction: Building accommodations that blend into the natural environment and
  • minimize impact, often using local, sustainable materials.
  •  Low-impact transportation: Providing and encouraging the use of low-impact transportation like
  • walking, cycling, or public transit for getting around.
  • Visitorandcommunitypractices
  •  Conservation and education: Educating visitors on the importance of conservation, local wildlife, and
  • respecting habitats. This includes following marked trails and not disturbing animals.
  •  Local economic benefits: Ensuring a significant portion of the revenue from tourism goes directly to
  • the local community and supporting local businesses and services.
  •  Cultural respect: Encouraging respectful interactions with local culture, such as respecting customs,
  • modesty in dress, and asking permission before taking photos.
  •  Visitor management: Using visitor management plans and guiding visitors to prevent overcrowding
  • and minimize negative impacts.
  • Operationalandpolicypractices
  •  Responsible operators: Choosing and supporting tour operators and accommodations that are
  • committed to sustainability and community well-being.
  •  Community involvement: Involving local communities in decision-making and ensuring they are
  • empowered and benefit fairly from tourism.
  •  Conservation funding: Directing revenue towards the conservation and management of natural areas.

questions.question: Illustrate the role of NGOs in ecotourism. / [CO2] [1x10 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Illustrate the role of NGOs in ecotourism. [An] / [CO2]
  • NGOs play a crucial role in ecotourism by acting as facilitators, advocates, and capacity builders to ensure
  • sustainability. They achieve this through community empowerment, conservation efforts, policy advocacy, and
  • raising awareness among local communities and tourists. NGOs also provide financial and technical support,
  • bridge the gap between communities and governments, and conduct research to inform responsible tourism
  • development.
